surfaces.part: main sign board with white 카페 lettering

answer.evidence: The whole sign is drawn face-on. Rows 1-2 are a 1-2 row lighter rim at the top of the header (#b27361 then #8b4f3f), with no front-edge line or eave shadow below it. Rows 3-5 are a white label panel and row 8 is a dark divider, so the header is a vertical face. Rows 9-27 are the vertical board with white lettering. Rows 28-30 are a flat grey-blue base strip with no horizontal surface visible. The width profile (12, 14, 16, 14, 16) only shows rounded corners and small steps, with no ellipse. No part shows a top surface, so this is a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small vertical café sign: a reddish-brown body with a lighter top cap and light lettering. It measures 8 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) but below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills, which matches the kiosk and vending references. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted dark brown and reads as a dark material tone rather than a black sticker line. The body carries about 4 lightness steps (highlight on the cap, light, mid, dark), and the lettering gives it some texture. The references have more small details, such as panels, windows and per-part highlights, so the candidate looks slightly thinner. As a simple single-tile sign it sits close to the lower end of the accepted shipped set (bus-shelter-a), but it is shallower than the kiosk and vending references. When in doubt, fail.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical brown signboard with a rounded top, a lighter face panel carrying the Korean text 카페, and a darker base. It reads as a standing prop and matches the kind. Its measured 8 visible tones per tile sit between bus-shelter-a (6) and kiosk-a (12), and well under vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted dark brown, not near-black. The board shows about 4 steps on the brown ramp (highlight edge, mid, dark, deep) and the text adds contrast, but there is little grain, no per-surface speckle and no small details like the kiosk's striped awning or the vending machine's items. It is a clean, simple piece with no big flat fills, but it looks thinner and less textured than kiosk-a and vending-a beside it. With only 8 tones against 12 and 20 for the richer references, I would not accept it as equal.
